sc_dimensionality.finding: SC is a 40-D MDS solution, NOT the 22-D ShapeComp space used elsewhere in the paper. Its first 22 columns retain only ~88.8% of this solution's variance, against the 95.05% the paper reports for the animal-silhouette space, so they are not verified to be the canonical ShapeComp coordinates. The authors' Figure8.m calls pdist(SC) on all 40 columns, so the published Figure 8D correlations are 40-D-reference correlations.

network_vs_shapecomp.target_semantics: MODEL vs MODEL. Pairwise-distance agreement between each official network's 22-D output and the official MDS coordinates. No human ratings are involved.
network_vs_shapecomp.train_test_status: The paper states the networks were trained on 800,000 of 950,000 GAN shapes and evaluated on 1000 untrained shapes; Figure 8D is that held-out comparison. Held-out from NETWORK training, but the MDS reference space itself was fitted on animal silhouettes, and these shapes have no human ratings.

stimulus_input_contract.paper_contract: 384x2 (x,y); per coordinate subtract the absolute minimum then divide by the resulting absolute maximum (range 0-1); first point is the minimum-x point
stimulus_input_contract.verdict: The deposited `c` arrays are RAW GAN contours, not the normalised network input. The published coordinates were produced from a normalised version that is not in this member, so any EarthGlyph arm scored on these contours differs from the official route in preprocessing as well as in descriptors.

shared_contract_compatibility.note: standardize() refuses self-intersecting rings rather than silently repairing them, so these two GAN shapes cannot enter an E0/E1/E3 gallery as-is. They still have published official coordinates.

overlap_with_human_rated_h1.comparison_space: contours on both sides pass through standardize() onto the shared 128-point contract, so identical published shapes match exactly; the SC check uses all 1000 published coordinate rows and needs no contour loading

usability.reason_cannot_score_new_shapes: These are published outputs for a fixed 1000-shape set. Scoring a new shape still needs the unobtainable 109-descriptor engine or the network weights.
usability.preprocessing_confound: Official coordinates came from min-max-normalised 384-point contours with a minimum-x start point; E0/E1/E3 use the shared 128-point centred/unit-RMS/CCW contract. A ranking disagreement on this gallery cannot be attributed to the descriptor alone.
